title: Priming signal latency run capture — week of 2026-07-14
content:
Meeting context: weekly run-capture focused on the 'priming signal' experiments we kicked off June->July. Goal: quantify first-token and p50/p95 latencies improvement from short-lived KV prefix priming across three regions (us-west1, europe-west1, ap-southeast1). This doc is a blend of notes from the Wednesday triage + Friday retrospective run-capture.

Attendees: Maya Chen (owner), Ravi Patel, Liam O'Connor, Sofia Alvarez, Noah Kim, ops rotation oncall (Avery).

High-level summary:
- Experiment type: opportunistic priming (pre-warm KV cache + tiny prefix perf cache) for new chat sessions from bursty/PLG traffic.
- Run window: 2026-07-08 00:00 -> 2026-07-13 23:59 UTC.
- Traffic profile: synthetic mix (60% small chats, 30% medium, 10% long) + sampled real traffic replay for validation.
- Key result: median first-token latency reduced by ~38% in us-west1 and ~33% in europe-west1; p95 improvement smaller ~12-18% depending on load. Cost overhead from priming ~+3.1% token-equivalent GPU time on-average for primed slots; in high-burst windows overhead spiked to +8–10%.

Run details and knobs tried:
- Priming duration: 30s, 60s, 120s window options. We primarily tested 60s as default.
- Priming intensity: 4 priming requests per slot (small prompts sampling common prefixes) vs 8 requests. 4 seemed to hit diminishing returns vs cost.
- Routing policy: only primed slots for PLG-tiers and anonymous-prod traffic (not enterprise SLAs) to avoid violating isolation.
- Cache eviction: LRU with sticky TTL tuned to 90s.
- Autoscaler interaction: enable priming on idle slots only when fleet_util < 40% to prevent priming during capacity pressure.

Metrics (aggregated):
- us-west1 (60s priming, 4 requests): first-token p50 down 38% (orig 260ms -> 160ms), p95 down 14% (orig 970ms -> 835ms).
- europe-west1 (60s priming): p50 down 33% (310ms -> 208ms), p95 down 12% (1100ms -> 968ms).
- ap-southeast1 (60s priming): p50 down 18% (420ms -> 344ms), p95 no clear improvement (slight +2–5% noise) — attributable to higher cross-region latency to priming orchestrator in this run.
- Cost: overall GPU-time-equivalent +3.1% across fleet; per-region variance us-west1 +2.3%, europe +3.8%, apac +6.9% during priming bursts.

Operational observations (incidents / anomalies):
- 2026-07-09 03:12 UTC: priming controller mis-sent priming jobs to enterprise-dedicated pool for ~3 min; caused SLA ticket INF-2143 (now linked). Root cause: routing policy default fallback path used wrong pool id when a cached config key was missing. Mitigation: rollback and pin route table; follow-up change in PR #57 to add a safety check and unit test.
- Inter-region clock skew (~80ms) caused some priming job timeouts in ap-southeast1 during the 60s window; we observed missing priming marks and therefore no latency improvement in some buckets. Ops note: add time-sync sanity checks to priming controller (ticket INF-2176).

Decisions made this week:
1) Keep 60s priming window as baseline for PLG traffic; 30s too noisy, 120s cost-prohibitive in low-util periods.
2) Default to 4 priming requests per slot; escalate only if p95 remains above target for a customer cohort.
3) Disable priming for dedicated enterprise pools until we add explicit opt-in via tenant config property.
4) Add a soft throttle: priming only when fleet_util <= 40% and regional-latency-signal OK.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Add route-table validation in priming controller to prevent sending to wrong pool (Ravi Patel) — ETA 2026-07-18.
- Time-sync sanity check + monitoring in priming agent (Liam O'Connor) — ETA 2026-07-20.
- Cost-model dashboard: per-region priming overhead and per-tenant cost attribution (Sofia Alvarez + Finance liaison) — ETA 2026-07-28.
- Create a small canary that runs priming for only 5% of PLG traffic with detailed tracing to verify apac behavior (Noah Kim) — ETA 2026-07-21.
- Postmortem write-up for INF-2143 (ops->ticket owner) (Maya Chen) — ETA 2026-07-16.

Notes to self / open questions: 
- Is priming actually masking a different root cause? Some traffic shapes (short chat bursts that come after longer idle spells) might be better solved with smarter slot prefetching rather than priming. We should compare against a 'predictive warm' model that uses traffic history per IP / tenant fingerprint.
- How does priming interact with quantized KV caches (8-bit paths) — do we lose representational fidelity and inadvertently increase inference variance? Follow-up: add a small AB test with quantized vs full-precision cache (ticket INF-2199).
- Can we make priming cheaper by replaying 1 token-worth of the real user's prefix (privacy implications) vs synthetic prefixes? Legal & privacy check required for using user-derived prefixes; escalate to security/compliance before any move.

Quick retrospective bullets (what worked / what didn't):
- Worked: clear p50 wins in core regions, easy rollback path, minimal complexity added to primary runtime.
- Didn't: apac results inconsistent, cost spikes in high-burst windows, initial route-table bug.

Suggested incremental experiments (next 2 sprints):
- Adaptive priming intensity: vary priming-requests-per-slot based on recent request size distribution (low-cost heuristic).
- Regional leader for priming orchestration to reduce inter-region control-plane traffic (one leader per continent).
- Short-duration predictive warmers that trigger based on simple heuristics (e.g., user session reappearance within X minutes).

Run artifacts / logs to inspect (internal):
- priming-controller logs: s3://redwood-ops-logs/priming/2026-07-08-2026-07-13/*
- perf capture: perfviz.us-west1/priming-july8-13.tar.gz
- linked PRs and tickets: see linked_artifacts above.

Meeting takeaway (one line): keep experiment in limited rollout for PLG traffic with tightened safety checks and a short canary in APAC to validate before rolling wider.

Appendix: shorthand checklist for oncall when priming is enabled:
- If p95 latency increases >10% after priming enabled in a region: toggle priming off for that region, escalate to infra-priming-thread, check priming-controller route table.
- If GPU utilization increases >7% with no p50 benefit: pause priming and capture 1h perf trace.
- If priming jobs appear in enterprise pools: immediate rollback and create incident ticket.

End of notes.
